title: DART crash reshapes asteroid orbit in seconds
description: In September 2022 the DART spacecraft deliberately collided with Dimorphos, shortening its orbit by thirty two minutes. This short documentary follows the final moments and the scientific breakthrough of humanity’s first asteroid deflection test.
hook_card: We hit an asteroid on purpose.

shots.narration: The final full image, taken two seconds before impact, shows Dimorphos’s rocky surface on 26 September 2022.
The DART spacecraft, a 570‑kilogram probe, speeds toward the 160‑metre moonlet orbiting Didymos.
Traveling at about 22,000 km/h, it closes the final two seconds before collision.
The impact shatters the surface, ejecting a bright plume of dust and rock into space.
The plume expands into a tail thousands of kilometres long, confirming high‑velocity material ejection.
From a safe distance, Italy’s LICIACube captures the debris cloud, providing the first close‑up view.
Scientists measure Dimorphos’s orbit shortened by 32 minutes, the 73‑second success threshold.
The collision demonstrates humanity’s first successful asteroid deflection, a milestone for planetary protection.
